title: Capture loss window: the volatile event stream cannot replay committed events

base.note: Reproduced at the accepted base before any code change, per the charter. This scenario is engine-derived at the Rust base, not an oracle receipt: the defect under test is the absence of a replay cursor, which no oracle run can emit.

preserves: bounded volatile SSE fan-out: a slow subscriber that overflows receives the sticky typed refusal, and even frames admitted to the bounded queue are discarded, never replayed
events published while a subscriber is absent reach no queue and never appear on any stream again
a reconnect yields only the connection frame and publishes from that moment on
protocol-v2 frame grammar: no SSE id, no retry field, event: message / data: only
intentionally_excludes: the durable store: the committed rows of the missed events and their bounded cursor recovery are the J02 contract
location/interest filtering: the host subscription uses the absent interest, so every frame reaches it; the location binding of the replay cursor is the J03 contract
wall-clock timing: the scenario is deterministic frame order with no timers, ambient clock or randomness

determinism.identifiers: Event ids are fixture-supplied (evt_*); this event kind carries no engine-minted timestamp on the wire.
determinism.network: No network or provider process is exercised; the hub is in-process.

record_contracts.actions: Ordered hub operations (subscribe, publish, read, reconcile) each with the observable frame or typed receipt it must produce. Operations are the hub's public surface (subscribe_host, publish, next_frame, reconcile), not private internals.
record_contracts.stream: The exact frame multiset each subscriber observes, its terminal outcome, and the missed-event markers proven absent from every stream.

evidence.claim: Executed at the accepted base: the loss window reproduces, and the volatile stream alone cannot replay the missed events.
